A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CROWDNOTES+ study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching analyses relocated between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original analysis of 30,791 health-related notes, experiments with 15 LLMs on HEALTHNOTES, ablations, evidence comparisons and judge-validation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a human preference evaluation comparing generated and human-written notes.

M1.justification: The augmentation and automation pipelines, utility-guided evidence selection, generation prompts, HEALTHJUDGE training objective and hierarchical evaluation remain unchanged. Section 4.2 condenses the existing procedure without introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English health-note corpus and 1,268-pair HEALTHNOTES benchmark. The new human evaluation uses cases from this retained benchmark, adding no domain, language or task coverage.

E2.justification: The human-written baseline, 15-model generation suite and helpfulness-judge comparators are retained. The new preference study compares existing o3, GPT-4.1 and MedGemma-27B configurations against the same human-written baseline, without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 adds a human evaluation protocol: three annotators compare 100 randomized, anonymized note pairs, balanced between 50 Helpful and 50 Not Helpful cases, using five quality criteria and aggregated votes. Existing retrieval controls, model configurations, training settings and length constraints remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new human preference study provides supplementary validation that automatically assessed note-quality advantages also appear in human judgments. The query-diversity and utility-judgment ablations, 89-note error analysis, and evidence-selection failure cases are retained; the latter analyses move from Appendix B into Section 7.3.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the single-run statement, temperature-zero setting and existing judge-agreement reporting. The new preference results introduce no confidence intervals, significance tests, repeated-run estimates or annotator-agreement statistics.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports human preference win rates of 87.0% for o3, 77.0% for GPT-4.1 and 62.0% for MedGemma-27B. Existing benchmark and ablation scores, evidence-utility results, judge-validation results and plotted findings remain unchanged after matching renumbered displays.

T1.justification: Equation (1), its conditional decomposition of relevance, correctness and helpfulness, and the candidate-pool and evidence-quota definitions are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain the latency bottleneck, the two-mode CROWDNOTES+ framework, HEALTHNOTES and HEALTHJUDGE, weaknesses in crowd helpfulness ratings, and improved note and evidence quality. The human preference study supplies additional support for an existing superiority claim.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 newly interprets human preferences as corroborating automatic evaluation and supporting better explanatory context. Existing interpretations of source credibility and retrieval failures, and limitations concerning English health content, reasoning capabilities and upstream detection, are retained with revised wording.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code-and-data repository pointer and specifies independent expert review of the 89 error cases in Section 7.1. Existing prompts, model identifiers and implementation settings are retained. Both versions still contain the controlled, research-only release statement; actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Changes such as Potthast 2017 to 2018, Xing 2025 to 2026, and the published venue for Li et al. update bibliographic records of already cited works.

P1.justification: v3 revises explanatory prose, discussion headings, the conclusion and limitations, and consolidates former Appendix B into Section 7.3. Author contact information and bibliography formatting also change. These refinements retain the overall narrative and main section sequence.

P2.justification: v3 adds the human-preference table and relocates Figures 7 and 8 from the appendix into the main discussion. Captions are revised, and Figure 8's fourth failure label becomes Insufficient Cross-Source Synthesis, matching the prose. Existing plotted data and other display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new human preference evaluation in Section 7.2 provides useful direct support for note quality beyond v2's automatic scoring and judge-validation checks. Consolidating evidence analyses and adding a code/data pointer also improve usability. The gain is limited by the 100-pair study's lack of uncertainty and annotator-agreement reporting; the underlying method and existing benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
